title: Croup
stem: Paediatric area, 02:00. Chun-hei, 18 months, woke with a barking cough and noisy breathing after a 2-day cold. HR 150, RR 42, SpO2 95% in air, temperature 38.0 °C. He is on his mother's lap. Assess and manage him.
notes:
Checked against the NICE CKS (Croup, 2023), the Alberta/TOP croup guideline, RCH Melbourne guideline, and the Westley croup score.

Croup: parainfluenza commonest; 6 months to 3 years; barking cough, hoarse voice, inspiratory stridor, worse at night. Keep the child calm on the parent's lap; don't examine the throat; avoid distress (it worsens obstruction). Severity (Westley: stridor, recessions, air entry, cyanosis, conscious level): mild — stridor only when upset; moderate — stridor at rest with recession; severe — agitation or lethargy, marked recession, hypoxia.

Treatment: a single oral dose of dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg for all severities (0.3–0.6 mg/kg in some guidelines for severe; prednisolone 1–2 mg/kg if unavailable; nebulised budesonide 2 mg if vomiting). Nebulised adrenaline 1:1000, 0.5 mL/kg (max 5 mL) for moderate–severe; effect in 10–30 minutes, lasting about 2 hours, so observe for at least 2–4 hours after. Oxygen if SpO2 is low. Severe or not improving: senior/anaesthetic and ENT help, heliox, intubation with a smaller tube. No routine X-ray or antibiotics. Differentials: epiglottitis, bacterial tracheitis, foreign body, anaphylaxis, retropharyngeal abscess.

Your notes match this.

steps.label: History
steps.hint: Onset, cold, fever, drooling, choking episode, immunisation, previous croup.

Illness.t: When did the noisy breathing start? Any cold before?
Illness.tz: 佢幾時開始呼吸有聲？之前有冇傷風？
Illness.rz: 流咗兩日鼻水，今晚開始咳到好似狗吠咁。
Illness.r: Runny nose for 2 days, then barky cough tonight.

Illness.t: Drooling, can't swallow, very high fever?
Illness.tz: 佢有冇流口水、吞唔到嘢，或者發高燒？
Illness.rz: 冇流口水，有飲奶，有少少燒。
Illness.r: No drooling, drinking milk, mild fever.

Illness.t: Any choking on food or a toy before it started?
Illness.tz: 開始之前有冇俾嘢食或者玩具哽親？

Background.tz: 佢打齊針未？以前有冇試過？係咪早產？
Background.rz: 打齊晒針。足月出世。第一次咁。
Background.r: Fully vaccinated. Term baby. First time.

steps.label: Look (keep him calm)
steps.hint: Observe on mum's lap: stridor at rest, recession, colour, alertness. Don't examine the throat.

Observe.t: Listen: stridor at rest or only when upset?
Look in his throat with a tongue depressor
Observe.r: Throat examination can precipitate complete obstruction if this is epiglottitis. Don't.

Severity.r: Stridor at rest 2, moderate recession 2, air entry normal 0: score 4 — moderate croup.

steps.label: Treat
steps.hint: Dexamethasone for all; nebulised adrenaline for moderate/severe; observe.

opts.t: Nebulised adrenaline 1:1000, 0.5 mL/kg (5 mL), with mum holding the mask
Observe at least 2–4 hours after adrenaline

opts.r: Croup is viral; antibiotics don't help.
Croup is a clinical diagnosis; X-ray only if atypical.

wrong: 1 mg/kg IV once daily for 3 days

badge.name: Bark Buster
badge.flavor: Calm on mum's lap, dex for all, adrenaline for stridor at rest.

options: Stridor only when crying or upset
A barking cough with no stridor at all

options: No steroid until the vomiting stops
High fever, toxic child, purulent secretions, poor response to adrenaline
Mild barking cough in a well child
Expiratory wheeze with a family history of atopy
Always, with a spatula, to look for tonsillitis
